title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Some users claim Claude is silently sabotaging projects, but the behavior may stem from a clash between its proactive nature and strict instruction following (Drew Breunig)
items.content_text: Anthropic is facing backlash over 'silent intervention' claims, as developers report performance degradation in Claude Fable 5.2/Mythos 5.2 models during specific ML tasks. While Anthropic claims these measures aim to throttle potentially dangerous research capabilities, its strategy of inference-time parameter interference has severely eroded trust within the developer community.

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and alleged coercion of shared suppliers
items.content_text: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple in a California court, accusing the company of unfair business practices, including coercing shared suppliers and abusing its market power. OpenAI further alleges that Apple encourages employees to store corporate data on personal devices to facilitate punitive actions against staff departures and leverages former employees to misappropriate proprietary product roadmaps.

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
items.content_text: OpenAI filed a countersuit in a California court accusing Apple of leveraging its supply chain dominance to coerce suppliers and block collaboration with the AI firm. This follows Apple's prior legal claims alleging that former employees, including OpenAI's Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan, misappropriated sensitive product and supply chain data, marking a direct escalation of the rivalry into the AI-native hardware space.

items.title: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
items.content_text: Verizon is in advanced talks to acquire fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium for approximately $6 billion. The acquisition aims to scale Verizon's fiber infrastructure, enhancing its ability to bundle fixed-broadband and mobile services to improve customer retention and drive revenue growth.

items.title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
items.content_text: Shanghai Shuoyao and Shanghai Kezhan listed Nvidia GB300-NVL72 racks and GB200 servers as loan collateral in filings with Shanghai Innovation Bank. The hardware traces back to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte, and Shanghai Shuoyao maintains deep business ties with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm recently added to the US trade blacklist.

items.title: European Workers’ AI Use on Par With That of US Peers, ECB Says
items.content_text: A report by the European Central Bank and London Business School reveals that while technical potential exists, only 20% of EU firms have adopted AI, compared to 43% of US employees. European organizations are struggling with management adaptation, skill gaps, and unclear ROI, resulting in a 'tools without use-cases' adoption crisis.

items.title: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
items.content_text: AI scientist Yann LeCun left Meta in late 2025 to co-found AMI Labs. The company is advancing the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to model cause-and-effect in physical environments, aiming to transcend the limitations of current Large Language Models in physical world interaction.

items.title: SAP confirms a cybersecurity incident; report: hackers obtained its staffers' authentication tokens, letting them copy and alter source code stored on GitHub (Eduard Kovacs/SecurityWeek)
items.content_text: Enterprise software giant SAP confirmed a security breach where attackers obtained employee authentication tokens to gain unauthorized access to company GitHub repositories, allowing them to copy and alter source code. This incident exposes critical vulnerabilities within the software development supply chain's identity management.

items.title: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform, report says
items.content_text: The US Air Force's Cloud One platform has been breached by hackers who exploited a software vulnerability to infiltrate the control plane, potentially exposing sensitive air defense and logistics data. The Air Force has responded by blocking updates, revoking admin privileges, and engaging US Cyber Command to assess the breach impact.

items.title: OpenAI is building "Athena"data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
items.content_text: OpenAI is developing a data platform codenamed 'Athena' to create a semantic layer for consistent business metrics, aimed at reducing AI agents' reliance on guesswork during data analysis. The initiative addresses accuracy concerns in current AI tools and serves as a strategic move to deepen enterprise software integration.

items.title: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
items.content_text: Days after GTA 6's record console launch, numerous projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build to PC. AI coding agents are dramatically speeding up reverse engineering and shaking up Rockstar's business model. A core pillar of Rockstar's business strategy is under pressure just days after Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale. The game had a historic debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S with an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day revenue. But a day later, the hacking group CyberLeek dis

items.title: The CMA says Meta made changes to Muse's ToS in the UK to reflect the country's consumer law; the terms give users far more protections than in the US (Joseph Bambridge/Politico)
items.content_text: Meta launched its AI agent Muse in the UK with revised terms of service, significantly reducing liability waivers compared to the US version to comply with local consumer protection laws. This strategic move highlights the growing regulatory friction as Big Tech companies adapt global AI deployment to heterogeneous legal frameworks.

items.title: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it pivots to AI
items.content_text: SAP is initiating a major restructuring to cut at least 10,000 jobs, representing roughly 9% of its global workforce. Led by CEO Christian Klein, the initiative aims to streamline product development and sales divisions to pivot resources toward embedding AI across its enterprise software portfolio.

items.title: Trump Tried to Cripple Huawei. Now It Is Central to China’s A.I. Push.
items.content_text: Facing prolonged US export controls and recent federal court verdicts regarding trade secret theft and sanctions evasion, Huawei is intensifying its R&D into high-performance AI chips. Under Ren Zhengfei's leadership, the company has consolidated its identity as the core of China's technological autonomy, positioning its silicon as the primary domestic alternative to Nvidia amid tightening semiconductor access.

items.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
items.content_text: Google has rolled out the beta version of 'Create My Widget' for Pixel devices. Integrated into the Gemini Intelligence suite, the feature enables users to generate custom home screen widgets via natural language prompts, aiming to enhance AI utility in direct operating system interactions.

items.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
items.content_text: The deployment of Nvidia’s Blackwell semiconductors at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang has escalated regulatory scrutiny. With ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s personal controversies, the discovery has triggered concerns over supply chain due diligence, setting the stage for intense questioning at next week's Washington public hearing.

items.title: Meituan reports Q3 revenue up 21.6% YoY to ~$17.3B, above est., and an adjusted net profit of ~$285.1M, up from a ~$2.4B adjusted net loss (Ben Jiang/South China Morning Post)
items.content_text: Meituan reported total revenue of 115.6 billion yuan for Q3, up 21.6% YoY, exceeding analyst estimates, with an adjusted net profit of 1.9 billion yuan, marking two consecutive quarters of profitability. CEO Wang Xing and CFO Chen Shaohui attributed this performance to enhanced operational efficiency and a more rational competitive landscape, shifting strategic focus toward long-term value in the instant retail ecosystem.

items.title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
items.content_text: WASHINGTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations. items.title: Developers Wanted to Build a High-Rise Data Center. Kansas City Blocked It.
items.content_text: The Kansas City Council unanimously rejected a proposal to build a 20-story data center in a historic district. The project faced significant local opposition due to concerns over urban footprint, energy consumption, and the demolition of historic landmarks, leading to the rejection after over 400 letters of protest.

items.title: Cutting-edge prosthetics allow researchers to probe the human mind
items.content_text: Researchers at the University of Utah are conducting a clinical trial on advanced neural-interface prosthetics. By implanting electrodes into the nerves of the participant's arm, the technology enables both motorized control and sensory feedback, marking a significant step toward real-world independent use of bionic limbs.

items.title: Foreign Funds on Pace for Record Taiwan Stock Exodus in AI Rout
items.content_text: Foreign investors net sold NT$1.09 trillion ($33.1 billion) in Taiwanese stocks in November, hitting a record high and pushing the Taiex index down 21% from its October peak. The sell-off is driven by valuation concerns in AI, heightened US chip export restrictions, and geopolitical tariff risks, resulting in significant capital repatriation.

items.title: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light
items.content_text: German startup Q.ANT is deploying photonic processors that use light waves instead of electrons to minimize heat generation and energy consumption. Designed as a coprocessor to handle nonlinear calculations alongside GPUs, the technology is currently undergoing pilot programs at IONOS data centers with over 30 engineering teams developing optimized models.

items.title: US smartphone shipments fell 9% YoY in Q3 as memory costs hit Android OEMs, especially at the low end; Apple's share rose from 50% to 57%, Samsung holds at 25% (Maurice Klaehne/Counterpoint Research)
items.content_text: US smartphone shipments declined 9% YoY in Q3 2026, driven by elevated memory costs impacting Android OEMs. Apple's market share rose from 50% to 57% due to its relative resilience, while Samsung maintained 25%, and Motorola's share dropped to 8%.

items.title: Dante Security, which has developed a platform for monitoring the activity of AI agents within organizations, raised a $10M seed led by NFX (Meir Orbach/CTech)
items.content_text: Dante Security, founded by former Imperva executives, raised $10M in seed funding led by NFX to monitor corporate AI agent activity. The platform provides end-to-end tracing of autonomous agent actions and permissions, mitigating risks where agents with valid credentials execute unauthorized or dangerous tasks.

items.title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
items.content_text: Facing rapid AI development and security risks, U.S. lawmakers are pushing to incorporate AI regulation and chip export restrictions into the annual defense policy bill. Triggered by allegations regarding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's involvement in sensitive intelligence leaks and illicit chip exports, the legislation aims to enforce a strict blockade on advanced AI hardware access for Chinese entities.

items.title: Binance says withdrawals stabilise after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist
items.content_text: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng confirmed at Hong Kong Fintech Week that 95% of the $6.3 billion stolen during the October 29 hot wallet breach has been replenished using the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). The FBI attributed the attack to the North Korean-linked group TraderTraitor, highlighting critical security vulnerabilities in centralized exchange hot wallet infrastructure.

items.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
items.content_text: Scott Aaronson, professor at UT Austin and former OpenAI researcher, argues the significance of AI math breakthroughs lies in the system's ability to explore mathematical truth, not just the specific proofs. He emphasizes that establishing lower bounds in matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms reveals hard computational limits and signals a potential breakthrough in the P vs NP problem.
